advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the added latency of serializing all full-route jobs behind `classify` is acceptable vs. the prior parallel-with-clear-vote design.
evidence: Removed comment previously said optionality was 'Independent of clear-vote/require-ticket so it runs fully parallel with build-and-test'
classify job does a Gerrit checkout + `--deepen` loop + sparse checkout of main before emitting `route`, and every full job waits on it
advisory.finding: All full-route jobs (build-and-test, mutation, optionality, artifact-probe, eval-discipline, golden-path, verify-identity) now list `classify` in `needs` and gate on its completion, so the common full route no longer starts in parallel with clear-vote/require-ticket but serializes behind an added runner job (checkout + deepen + sparse-checkout + python). This adds start-up latency to every non-docs change.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether a transient classifier failure should block Verified despite a green full fallback route, or whether the full route's success should count when classify fails.
evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml:468 `needs.classify.result == 'success' &&` gates the entire CONCLUSION truth branch
Full jobs' `if` uses `needs.classify.result != 'success' || ... == 'full'` so they DO run when classify fails
CONTRIBUTING.md states 'A classifier failure also starts the full fallback route and still blocks Verified' — this is documented intent, but the fallback route's work is then wasted
advisory.finding: A transient failure of the `classify` job forces the Verified vote to 'failure' even when the full fallback route runs and all full jobs pass, because the CONCLUSION guard requires `needs.classify.result == 'success'`. Full jobs run on classifier failure (their `if` fallback), yet their green result cannot produce a Verified +1.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test invoking classifier.main([...]) that asserts stdout is exactly the route token and exit code is 0 (capsys), for both docs-only and full repositories.
evidence: gerrit-verify.yaml classify step: `route="$(python3 .trusted-verify-router/scripts/classify_gerrit_verify_change.py --repository "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE")"` — the workflow validates only `docs-only|full`, so stdout format IS the contract
advisory.finding: The classifier's main() CLI entrypoint — the actual contract the Gerrit workflow consumes via `route="$(python3 .../classify_gerrit_verify_change.py --repository ...)"` (gerrit-verify.yaml route step) — is never invoked by any test. Tests call classify_repository/classify_paths/classify_paths0 directly but never exercise main(), so the stdout format (a bare `docs-only`/`full` line with no prefix/trailing noise), the --repository argument parsing, and the exit code 0 are unverified. A regression that added a log prefix to stdout, changed the default repository, or broke argparse would route silently to `full` classification failure downstream without failing any test.
scenarios: A refactor adds an informational log line to stdout, so the workflow's `case "$route"` sees an invalid multi-line route and fails classification
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a capsys-based test calling classifier.main(['--repository', str(repo)]) on a docs-only and a code tree, asserting captured stdout.strip() equals DOCS_ONLY / FULL and the return value is 0.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral test that runs the docs-contract selector's bash body against a synthetic tree, asserting it selects */test_*.py, excludes integration/external/conftest paths, and exits 1 with the documented ::error:: message when the selection is empty.
evidence: .github/actions/docs-gates/action.yml:157-158: `if [ "${#doc_tests[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then` / `echo "::error::documentation contract selector found no tests"`
tests/unit/test_gerrit_docs_only.py asserts only text presence: `assert "git grep -Il" in action`, `assert "tests/integration/" in action` — no execution of the selector
test_gate_step_tree_skew _SCRIPT_RE matches only `scripts/*.py`; this step's run: has no such token so it is not collected/executed
advisory.finding: The docs-gates composite action's 'Documentation contract tests' step contains untested selection logic: a git-grep-driven selector, a case filter that must exclude tests/integration/*, tests/external/*, and */conftest.py while keeping */test_*.py, and an empty-selection error path (`::error::documentation contract selector found no tests` then `exit 1`). This step carries no `scripts/*.py` token, so the test_gate_step_tree_skew sweep does not execute it, and no other test exercises the selector or its fail-on-empty contract. The only related assertions (test_gerrit_docs_only.py) grep the action text for `git grep -Il`, `tests/integration/`, `not integration and not external` — presence checks, not behavior. A regression that inverted the case filter (selecting integration tests into the reduced lane) or dropped the empty-set guard would pass every test.
scenarios: The case exclusion is edited to accidentally admit tests/integration/* into the docs-only lane
The empty-selection `exit 1` guard is removed, letting a mis-scoped selector silently run zero tests and pass
